title: Butter Chicken
subtitle: Delhi makhani chicken in tomato and cream sauce
excerpt: The most widely eaten Indian dish in the world: tandoor-charred chicken pieces simmered in a silky, butter-enriched tomato sauce with cream, fenugreek, and warm spices. Mild, rich, and deeply satisfying.

recipe.sourceNotes: Butter chicken (murgh makhani) was created in Delhi in the 1950s at Moti Mahal restaurant by Kundan Lal Gujral, who combined leftover tandoori chicken with a buttery tomato sauce to create a dish for the restaurant's high-profile guests. It became the template for the whole genre of makhani (buttery) dishes, including dal makhani. The sauce is characterised by its smoothness (always blended and passed through a sieve), its richness (from butter and cream), and its distinctive flavour from dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi), which are rubbed between the palms and crumbled in at the end. The sauce is intentionally mild; the chicken is marinated in spiced yoghurt and charred before being added, providing the contrasting depth.

content.text: The dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi) are essential; the dish tastes measurably different without them. Rub them between your palms before adding to release their fragrance. Blend and pass the sauce through a sieve for the characteristic silky texture. Add the cream off the heat to prevent it separating.

content.text: Mix the chicken with the yoghurt, half the ginger, 3 minced garlic cloves, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp coriander, paprika, and 1 tsp salt. Marinate for at least 30 minutes. Cook the marinated chicken under a hot grill or in a hot pan until charred at the edges and cooked through, about 12 to 15 minutes. Set aside.

Make the sauce: heat the butter and oil in a pan. Cook the onion for 10 minutes until golden. Add the remaining garlic and ginger, the remaining cumin and coriander, and garam masala. Stir for 1 minute. Add the tinned tomatoes and sugar. Simmer for 20 minutes. Blend until smooth and pass through a sieve. Return to the pan.

Add the cooked chicken to the sauce. Simmer gently for 10 minutes. Remove from the heat. Stir in the cream and crushed fenugreek leaves. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve with naan bread or steamed rice and scattered with coriander.
